q: Why is F-Log2 noisy in the dark areas?
a: Log footage such as F-Log2 is noisy in the shadows, and lifting them in a grade makes the noise more visible; so reduce noise before the correction that lifts the shadows. Spatial NR averages each pixel with similar pixels in the same frame, which also softens fine detail; temporal NR averages the same point over neighbouring frames, removing noise while keeping detail, best for static or slow shots.

q: How do I set up a spatial NR node?
a: 1. Add a node at the start of the chain (Insert Node Before on the first node, `grade.insertNode`): NR works best before contrast and saturation. 2. Open the Noise tab. 3. Raise NR luma for grainy brightness noise and NR chroma for coloured blotches, starting around 0.3, and compare with the node switched off. 4. NR radius (0.25 … 3.5 source pixels) sets how far it looks for similar neighbours: larger is smoother and slower. 5. To clean only part of the picture, add a window to the same node.

q: In Resolve I'd use Spatial NR on a node. How do I do that in Revolution?
a: Insert a node at the start of the grade and use its Noise tab: NR luma, NR chroma and NR radius (`nr.luma`, `nr.chroma`, `nr.size` with `grade.setParam`). It's one edge-preserving filter with two strengths and a radius, fewer modes than Resolve's palette.

q: When does temporal NR actually render?
a: Temporal NR is a setting of the clip, applied right after the input colour transform, before every node and effect. Select the clip, then use the Temporal NR section in Effect Controls (Inspector in the Resolve workflow) or the Temporal NR (clip) block in the Color page's Noise tab: Enabled on, Luma and Chroma (0.5 is a good start, 1.0 strong), Frames 1 or 2 each side, Motion (default 0.5). It renders at export, Export Frame, in the render cache and on the paused Program frame, not while playing.

q: What does the Motion setting in temporal NR do?
a: Luma (brightness noise) and Chroma (colour noise): 0.5 is a good start, 1.0 is strong. Frames is how many frames on each side are averaged: 1 (three in all) or 2 (five, cleaner and slower). Motion (0 … 1, default 0.5) is how much disagreement in the motion estimate is accepted: lower it if moving edges ghost, raise it for more cleaning on difficult slow motion.

q: Does Paste Grade copy temporal NR?
a: Paste Grade doesn't, because temporal NR isn't part of the grade. Use Clip ▸ Temporal NR ▸ Copy / Paste Temporal NR (`tnr.copy`, `tnr.paste`), or Paste Attributes (its `temporalNr` option is on by default).

q: In Resolve I'd use Temporal NR in Motion Effects. How do I do that in Revolution?
a: Temporal NR is a clip setting here, not a node: Effect Controls (Inspector) ▸ Temporal NR, or the Noise tab's Temporal NR (clip) block. It has two strengths, 1 or 2 frames each side and one motion tolerance, and renders at export, in the render cache and on the paused frame.

q: How does the spatial noise filter keep edges sharp?
a: Spatial is an edge-preserving bilateral filter: each pixel is averaged with neighbours weighted by distance and similarity, so real edges are left alone; luma and colour are filtered separately and the filter size follows the picture size. Temporal estimates motion with dense pyramidal Lucas–Kanade optical flow on a small brightness copy, warps each neighbour onto the frame and blends it with a weight that falls as it differs, counting less where forward and backward motion disagree. It uses only the clip's own frames, never across a cut.

q: Does a Source monitor frame export include temporal NR?
a: Temporal NR applies to the whole picture of the clip: windows and qualifiers can't limit it, and a frame exported from the Source monitor has none (it isn't a timeline clip). Spatial NR costs GPU time, about 3–20 ms per 1080p frame on the RX 6700 XT depending on the radius and much more on an Intel GPU, so use a lower playback resolution while grading.

q: Does temporal NR still work during a transition?
a: Yes: during a transition the clips keep their temporal NR; the frames shown from their handles have neighbours within the transition.

q: Which parameters control noise reduction from a script?
a: Spatial, per node with `grade.setParam`: `nr.luma`, `nr.chroma` (0…1), `nr.size` (σ in source pixels). Temporal, per clip with `tnr.set` (e.g. `{"param": "luma", "value": 0.5}`): `luma`, `chroma`, `frames` (1 or 2), `motion`; plus `tnr.toggle`, `tnr.reset`, `tnr.toggleAnimation`, `tnr.moveKeyframe`, `tnr.get`. `grade.setParam` refuses the old `tnr.*` keys.
